claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

Let me start with: **Do you have a child (or children) that you're responsible for?** If yes, could you tell me how many children you have and their ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child. His name is Alex and he's 19 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex is 19 years old, I need to ask some additional questions as Child Benefit eligibility can extend beyond age 16 in certain circumstances.

**Is Alex currently in full-time non-advanced education or approved training?** (For example, studying for A-levels, Scottish Highers, or similar qualifications at school or college)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. Alex is studying for his A-levels at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know. I have a few more questions to determine eligibility.

**When did Alex turn 19, or when will he turn 20?** I need to understand his exact age in relation to his education, as there are specific age limits that apply even when a young person is in full-time education.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He turned 19 in February this year, so he won't be 20 until next February.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Now I need to understand your relationship to Alex and your living situation.

**Are you Alex's parent or the person responsible for him?** And **does Alex live with you, or do you contribute to his upkeep?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm his parent and he lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. I need to ask a few more questions about your circumstances:

**Do you normally live in the UK?** (This includes England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in England - in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is there anyone else also claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (For example, another parent or guardian)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, there's no one else claiming for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me ask one final question to complete my assessment:

**When does Alex's A-level course end, or when is he expected to finish his studies?** I need to know if he'll be continuing past his 20th birthday or finishing before then.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He'll be finishing his A-levels in June next year, so before he turns 20.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! **You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why: Child Benefit can continue for young people aged 16-19 who are in approved full-time education or training. Since Alex is 19, studying for his A-levels (which qualifies as approved education), and will complete his course before turning 20, he meets the criteria. You're his parent, he lives with you in the UK, and no one else is claiming for him.

You can continue to receive Child Benefit for Alex until:
- He finishes his A-levels in June next year, or
- The last Monday in August following his 19th birthday (whichever comes later)

Since he turned 19 in February this year, you can claim until at least the end of August following his completion of A-levels. If you're not already claiming, you should apply as soon as possible. If you're already receiving Child Benefit for Alex, it should continue automatically while he remains in education until the appropriate end date.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
